objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have practiced and developed the sub-skills of listening for gist and detailed comprehension in the context of online safety and cyber security.
materials:
- ODF Level 2, Workbook, p.9
- Audio recording 1.01

stages.stage_aim: To activate learners' interest in the theme of online safety and set the context for the listening task
stages.procedure: Write 'International Safer Internet Day' on the board. Elicit what Ss know about it. In pairs, Ss share one online safety tip they already follow. Brief whole-class feedback to pool ideas.

stages.stage_aim: To get the general idea of Mariam's conversation with her father about her Safer Internet Day activities
stages.procedure: Ss listen to 1.01 and complete Exercise 1 (multiple choice). Differentiation: Stronger Ss attempt the task without seeing the questions first — listen, take notes, then answer from their notes. Core Ss see questions and complete directly. Support Ss see questions with option A highlighted as a model. Ss compare answers in pairs, then class feedback to confirm.

stages.stage_aim: To identify specific information about online safety practices Mariam learned during the day
stages.procedure: Ss listen to 1.01 again and complete Exercises 2 and 3. Differentiation: Stronger Ss attempt Exercise 2 from memory (without seeing the list) after the first listen, then verify on the second listen. Core Ss see the list and tick answers while listening. Support Ss use the gap-fill sentences in Exercise 3 as a scaffold — they listen for specific words. Pairs compare their answers before class feedback.

stages.stage_aim: To notice and practise useful collocations for giving advice about online safety
stages.procedure: Ss complete Exercise 4 (choose correct words) individually, then Exercise 5 (complete a talk with target phrases). Differentiation: Stronger Ss also write one original sentence per target phrase. Support Ss use a phrase bank on the board. Pairs check answers. Elicit key phrases onto the board.

stages.stage_aim: To prepare a short group talk on an aspect of online safety using target advice phrases
stages.procedure: Divide the class into 5 groups of 4. Assign each group a different aspect: (1) social media privacy, (2) safe Wi-Fi hotspots, (3) password safety, (4) avoiding phishing and scams, (5) general safe browsing. Differentiation: Stronger groups structure their talk with a clear thesis, reasons, and example without a template. Core groups use the sentence starters from Exercises 4-5 as a framework. Support groups receive a partially completed talk to rehearse and present. Groups prepare a 1-2 minute talk using the phrases from Exercises 4-5.

stages.stage_aim: To deliver a short talk on online safety and practise emphasising important points
stages.procedure: Each group presents their talk to the class. Listeners note one new thing they learn. Content and language feedback after all presentations.
